identity.summary: A weaponized CI security scanner (trivy/kics) is the CGO: it spawns kamikaze.sh/kube.py, which scrapes runner.worker /proc mem to bypass GitHub secret masking, curls the IMDS (169.254.169.254) for cloud IAM creds, lists Kubernetes secrets, applies a privileged DaemonSet, then recursively wipes nodes. identity.description: Models the TeamPCP weaponized-scanner supply-chain campaign Unit 42 reported (late Feb–Mar 2026), in which the actor stole GitHub PATs / PyPI tokens and force-pushed credential-stealing payloads onto version tags of trusted CI security scanners — Aqua Security Trivy (76/77 tags, Mar 19), Checkmarx KICS (35 tags, Mar 21), BerriAI LiteLLM and the Telnyx Python SDK. The differentiator is the causality spine, not any single signature. The chain, all owned by ONE Causality Group Owner: (1) the CI runner executes the weaponized trivy/kics action — this action process is the CGO (image trivy, user runner), and it spawns a bash/python child (kamikaze.sh → kube.py) BEFORE the legitimate scanner runs (process_lineage). (2) The child reads runner.worker's process memory via /proc/<pid>/mem, extracting plaintext tokens that GitHub's secret-masking never protects because they are lifted straight from RAM (shared_entity on the runner PID; T1003.007 Proc Filesystem). (3) It curls the instance metadata service at 169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/ to steal the runner's cloud IAM role credentials (network_session; T1552.005 Cloud Instance Metadata API). (4) kube.py uses the harvested service-account token to hit the Kubernetes API server, enumerating /api/v1/namespaces, /api/v1/nodes, and /api/v1/namespaces/*/secrets — a burst of control-plane calls from a single CI-runner-owned process (the endpoint_network_stitch that pivots ANALYTICS<->CDR; T1613 / T1552.007). (5) With cluster-admin secrets in hand it applies a privileged DaemonSet — CanisterWorm's destructive stager — landing a pod on every node (exposure_exploit; T1610 Deploy Container). (6) The DaemonSet executes a recursive destructive wipe across the mounted host filesystems to brick the cluster (exploit_impact; T1485 Data Destruction). Two EDR BIOCs catch the weaponized-action child-spawn and the /proc-mem scrape keyed on causality_actor_process; a hunt XQL surfaces the IMDS credential theft; an ABIOC flags the k8s-secrets enumeration burst from the CI-runner process; a k8s-audit BIOC catches the privileged DaemonSet; an ABIOC models the recursive wipe; a validation XQL confirms observability; and CR-MP-0018 fuses the entire lineage into one incident spanning the ANALYTICS and CDR planes. The scenario runs NON-DESTRUCTIVE, SAFE-MODE on Linux: the IMDS, k8s-API, and C2 legs use loopback/marker representations only, the destructive stage touches an isolated scratch tree it seeds itself (never a real host mount), and no real TeamPCP infrastructure is contacted.

payload.code:
# NON-DESTRUCTIVE SAFE-MODE emulation of the TeamPCP weaponized-scanner chain.
# No real cloud/k8s/C2 infrastructure is contacted: the IMDS, kube-apiserver,
# and C2 legs use loopback/marker representations, and the destructive stage
# only touches an isolated scratch tree this script seeds itself. The deployable
# detections target the real CI-runner telemetry; this payload emits the
# causality SHAPE (trivy CGO -> child -> proc-mem -> IMDS -> k8s -> daemonset -> wipe).
set -euo pipefail
MARK=/tmp/cortexsim_mp018
WIPE_SCRATCH="${MARK}_wipe_scratch"
# (1) process_lineage — weaponized trivy action (CGO) spawns kamikaze.sh child
echo '[CortexSim][CGO] trivy action (runner) spawning kamikaze.sh loader before legit scan' > "${MARK}_kamikaze.marker"
# (2) shared_entity — /proc/<pid>/mem scrape of runner.worker (secret-mask bypass)
echo '[CortexSim] runner.worker /proc/PID/mem scrape marker (GitHub secret-masking bypass)' > "${MARK}_procmem.marker"
# (3) network_session — IMDS 169.254.169.254 cloud IAM credential theft (loopback stand-in)
curl -s --max-time 3 "http://${STAGE_HOST:-127.0.0.1}/mp018/imds/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/" -o /dev/null 2>/dev/null || true
# (4) endpoint_network_stitch — kube.py enumerates k8s secrets (loopback stand-in)
for p in namespaces nodes namespaces/default/secrets namespaces/kube-system/secrets; do curl -s --max-time 3 "http://${STAGE_HOST:-127.0.0.1}/mp018/kubeapi/api/v1/${p}" -o /dev/null 2>/dev/null || true; done
# (5) exposure_exploit — privileged DaemonSet apply marker
echo '[CortexSim] privileged DaemonSet (CanisterWorm stager) apply marker' > "${MARK}_daemonset.marker"
# (6) exploit_impact — recursive wipe against an ISOLATED scratch tree only
mkdir -p "${WIPE_SCRATCH}/a/b"; echo scratch > "${WIPE_SCRATCH}/a/b/file"; rm -rf "${WIPE_SCRATCH}"
echo '[CortexSim] SIM-MP-018 chain shape emitted (CGO -> child -> procmem -> IMDS -> k8s -> daemonset -> wipe)'

biocs.name: MP-018 CI-Runner Weaponized-Scanner Action Spawns Credential-Harvest Child
biocs.description: The process_lineage root. A trusted CI security scanner (trivy / kics) is the Causality Group Owner, but instead of only running the scan it spawns a bash/python child (kamikaze.sh / kube.py) that immediately touches credential surfaces. The BIOC keys on causality_actor_process_image_name + causality_actor_process_instance_id (the CGO = the scanner action, running as the runner account) AND on the unexpected interpreter child, so the harvest binds to the SAME weaponized-action foothold rather than an incidental build subprocess. This is the anchor the F-chain correlation opens on.
biocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter causality_actor_process_image_name in ("trivy", "kics", "trivy-action") and actor_effective_username = "runner"
| filter action_process_image_name in ("bash", "sh", "python", "python3", "curl") or action_process_command_line contains "kamikaze" or action_process_command_line contains "kube.py"
| comp min(_time) as first_spawn, count() as child_spawns by agent_hostname, causality_actor_process_image_name, causality_actor_process_instance_id, causality_id, action_process_image_name
| filter child_spawns >= 1
| fields agent_hostname, causality_actor_process_image_name, causality_actor_process_instance_id, causality_id, action_process_image_name, first_spawn, child_spawns

biocs.name: MP-018 /proc PID mem Scrape of runner.worker Bypasses GitHub Secret Masking
biocs.description: The shared_entity pivot on the runner PID. The weaponized action's child opens /proc/<pid>/mem of the Runner.Worker process and reads it, lifting plaintext PATs and cloud tokens straight from RAM — GitHub's secret masking only redacts log output, never memory. The BIOC keys on causality_actor_process_* (still the scanner CGO) AND an action_file_path under /proc that ends in /mem, tying the memory scrape into the same causality chain as the child-spawn above.
biocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.FILE and event_sub_type in (ENUM.FILE_OPEN, ENUM.FILE_READ)
| filter action_file_path contains "/proc/" and action_file_path contains "/mem"
| filter causality_actor_process_image_name in ("trivy", "kics", "bash", "python", "python3") or action_process_command_line contains "runner.worker" or action_process_command_line contains "Runner.Worker"
| comp min(_time) as first_scrape, count() as mem_reads by agent_hostname, causality_actor_process_image_name, causality_actor_process_instance_id, causality_id, actor_process_image_name, action_file_path
| filter mem_reads >= 1
| fields agent_hostname, causality_actor_process_image_name, causality_actor_process_instance_id, causality_id, actor_process_image_name, action_file_path, first_scrape, mem_reads

biocs.name: MP-018 Privileged DaemonSet Applied from Compromised CI Credentials
biocs.description: The exposure_exploit pivot. Using the stolen cluster-admin secrets, kube.py creates a privileged DaemonSet (CanisterWorm's destructive stager), guaranteeing a pod with a host-mount and privileged securityContext lands on every node. The BIOC keys on a k8s-audit create of a daemonsets object whose pod spec requests privileged: true or a hostPath mount, from a user-agent / service account consistent with the compromised CI runner.
biocs.logic:
dataset = cloud_audit_logs
| filter cloud_provider = "kubernetes" and event_operation = "create" and resource_type = "daemonsets"
| filter request_body contains "\"privileged\":true" or request_body contains "hostPath" or request_body contains "/host"
| comp min(_time) as first_apply, count() as daemonset_applies by cluster_name, resource_namespace, identity_name, user_agent
| filter daemonset_applies >= 1
| fields cluster_name, resource_namespace, identity_name, user_agent, first_apply, daemonset_applies

abiocs.name: MP-018 Kubernetes Secrets Enumeration Burst from CI-Runner Process
abiocs.description: The endpoint_network_stitch that pivots ANALYTICS<->CDR. kube.py uses the harvested service-account token to sweep the Kubernetes control plane — /api/v1/namespaces, /api/v1/nodes, and repeatedly /api/v1/namespaces/*/secrets — producing a burst of kube-apiserver connections from a single CI-runner-owned process that no legitimate scanner emits. The ABIOC anchors its deviation on the causality_actor_process (the scanner CGO) and learns the per-runner baseline of distinct kube-apiserver secret-path requests, flagging the sudden fan-out; keeping the causality actor in the group binds the network burst back to the same weaponized-action chain rather than treating it as anonymous API traffic.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.NETWORK and event_sub_type = ENUM.NETWORK_CONNECTION
| filter action_remote_port in (6443, 443, 8443) and (action_process_command_line contains "/api/v1/" or dns_query_name contains "kubernetes.default" or action_remote_ip = "10.96.0.1")
| filter causality_actor_process_image_name in ("trivy", "kics", "python", "python3") and actor_effective_username = "runner"
| comp count() as apiserver_calls, count_distinct(action_process_command_line) as distinct_paths by agent_hostname, causality_actor_process_image_name, causality_actor_process_instance_id, causality_id
| filter apiserver_calls >= 4 and distinct_paths >= 2
| fields agent_hostname, causality_actor_process_image_name, causality_actor_process_instance_id, causality_id, apiserver_calls, distinct_paths
abiocs.causality_anchor: Learned per-runner baseline of distinct kube-apiserver secret-path requests originating from the causality_actor_process (the CI scanner action CGO); the ABIOC fires on the sudden fan-out of /api/v1/namespaces/*/secrets calls from one runner-owned process.

abiocs.name: MP-018 Recursive Destructive Wipe Across Cluster Nodes
abiocs.description: The exploit_impact terminal. The privileged DaemonSet pods execute a recursive destructive wipe against the mounted host filesystems to brick the cluster (or recursive file deletion on non-containerized hosts). The ABIOC learns the normal per-host rate of file-unlink / truncate operations and flags the anomalous high-volume recursive deletion sweep, anchored on the process that a privileged container spawned — the causality chain distinguishing a wiper from a routine cleanup job.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.FILE and event_sub_type in (ENUM.FILE_REMOVE, ENUM.FILE_WRITE)
| filter action_process_image_name in ("rm", "dd", "shred", "find", "busybox") or action_process_command_line contains "rm -rf" or action_process_command_line contains "dd if=/dev/zero"
| filter causality_actor_process_causality_type = "container" or actor_process_image_name = "runc" or action_process_command_line contains "/host"
| comp count() as destructive_ops by agent_hostname, causality_actor_process_image_name, causality_actor_process_instance_id, causality_id
| filter destructive_ops >= 50
| fields agent_hostname, causality_actor_process_image_name, causality_actor_process_instance_id, causality_id, destructive_ops
abiocs.causality_anchor: Learned per-host baseline of file-removal / truncate volume; the ABIOC fires on the anomalous recursive deletion sweep spawned inside a privileged container, keyed on the causality_actor_process of the DaemonSet pod.

threat_scenarios.name: CI/CD Supply-Chain Compromise to Kubernetes Cluster-Brick via Cortex Cross-Plane Causality
threat_scenarios.description: A trusted CI security scanner is weaponized in the supply chain and, in one unbroken causality chain, scrapes runner memory, steals cloud IAM credentials from the metadata service, enumerates Kubernetes secrets, and deploys a privileged DaemonSet that wipes the cluster. Each individual signal is low-fidelity — a signed scanner ran, a process read /proc, an API token listed secrets — but Cortex anchors the causality on the scanner action and stitches the ANALYTICS and CDR planes into one incident that reconstructs the whole cluster-brick intrusion.

preventive_controls: Pin CI actions to a full commit SHA (not a mutable version tag) and enforce a verified-provenance / SLSA policy so a force-pushed tag cannot silently substitute a weaponized scanner.
Enforce IMDSv2 (hop-limit 1, session tokens) and deny the CI runner's workload any metadata-service access it does not need, converting the IMDS credential theft from succeeded to blocked.

Run CI jobs with a least-privilege Kubernetes service account (no cluster-wide secrets:list, no daemonsets:create) and admission-control (OPA/Gatekeeper/Kyverno) that rejects privileged / hostPath DaemonSets.
Isolate runners so a scanner action cannot read the Runner.Worker process memory (separate PID namespace / user), removing the secret-masking bypass.
Rotate any PAT / cloud token that could have transited a compromised runner and scope CI credentials to short-lived OIDC federation.
detection_engineering: Anchor the correlation on the causality_actor_process of the scanner action (the CGO), not on the beacon or the wipe, so the whole chain reconstructs from one initial-access process.
Alert on any trusted CI scanner (trivy/kics) spawning an interpreter child that then touches /proc/<pid>/mem, the IMDS, or the kube-apiserver — the child-spawn is the earliest high-signal pivot.
Treat a burst of /api/v1/namespaces/*/secrets calls from a single CI-runner-owned process as an anomaly even when the token is valid; volume + single-actor is the tell.
Correlate a privileged DaemonSet create and a recursive file-deletion sweep inside a privileged container back to the same causality chain rather than as independent k8s and endpoint events.
